test_title: PYST 06: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate homonym.

He will** bat** for his friend's innocence.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Support**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"bat"** in English can have multiple meanings depending on its context. It is a homonym (a word with the same spelling or pronunciation but different meanings). (समरूप शब्द)

 
 
• **English Meaning:** In this context, "bat" is used as a verb meaning "to support or defend someone or something."
 
• **Hindi Meaning:** समर्थन करना या बचाव करना।
 
• **Example:** The lawyer will bat for his client in the court of law.
 
 
 
• **Correct word explanation:** "Support" means to stand by or assist someone or something, often in difficult situations. (समर्थन करना)
 
 
• **Example:** She always supports her friends when they are in need.
 
 
 
• Hence, in the given sentence, "He will bat for his friend's innocence" means he will support or defend his friend regarding their innocence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Support**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Criticize **(आलोचना करना): To express disapproval of someone or something by pointing out faults or flaws.

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher criticized the student's essay for its lack of structure.
 
 
 
• **Play cricket **(क्रिकेट खेलना): To participate in the sport of cricket.
 
 
• **Example:** We often play cricket in the park during the weekends.
 
 
 
• **Hit** (मारना): To strike someone or something with force.
 
 
• **Example:** He hit the ball so hard that it went over the fence.
 
 

6c:T1085,
The correct answer is **Option 1**.</di
